extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automatic phonetic transcription generation followed by manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: text phonemizer of the CoML lab and whisper-timestamped model
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors made a deliberate effort to mitigate bias and increase representativeness by recruiting a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance body-conducted speech analysis and aid in creating robust communication systems for real-world use.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves the collection of personal data from participants, specifically including gender, though the data is anonymized and encrypted in compliance with GDPR.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for fundamental speech processing tasks, specifically Speech Enhancement, Speech-to-Phonemes, and Speaker Verification.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split by speaker into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets, ensuring that male and female speakers were balanced across the splits and preventing any speaker overlap.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio signals were preprocessed with a 20 Hz high-pass filter. Text transcripts were normalized by lowercasing and removing most punctuation. The data was then cleaned using three automatic filters to discard deficient samples based on Phoneme Error Rate (PER > 10%), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR > 1.5 dB), and sensitivity drift. Finally, audio segments were trimmed and adjusted based on Voice Activity Detection (VAD) timestamps.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: From this normalized text, we also generated the corresponding phonetic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)... A phase of manual phonetic transcription was then necessary for these unrecognized words, such as " algorithme ".

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Finally, to increase the representativeness and inclusivity of the dataset, a deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We hope this release will drive progress in body-conducted speech analysis and support the development of robust communication systems for real-world applications.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: ...governs the processing and protection of personal data... ensuring anonymization and encryption of data during storage and analysis. [...] a deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Using Vibravox has proven to yield satisfactory results in Speech Enhancement, Speech-to-Phonemes and Speaker Verification, which are three fundamental speech processing tasks.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: The dataset is then split by speaker, with 80% of male and female speakers in the training set, 10% in the development/validation set, and 10% in the test set. This ensures that all utterances from a given speaker are grouped together, preventing any speaker overlap between splits.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To enhance audio data quality, a 20 Hz high-pass filter is uniformly applied to each acquisition channel... we applied common text normalization operations, such as lowercasing text and removing punctuation except for apostrophes... we applied a series of three automatic filters to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies... The first filter discards any audio samples where PER[j] > 10%... The second filter... SNR[i, j] > 1.5 dB... the timestamps generated by Voice Activity Detection (VAD) are extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides. In rare cases where the adjusted start or end timestamps exceed the original audio boundaries, the audio is trimmed by 15 ms on the affected side.
